newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen higher as bond market tone firms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen higher as bond market tone firms.

text.p: A firmer tone in the U.S. Treasury market is expected to help Wall Street stocks move higher at Tuesday's open.

On Monday, slumping bonds pushed long-term yields up near the key seven percent level and dragged stocks lower in one of the slowest sessions of the year. Analysts said the fact that bonds held that level augured well for today's outlook.
"Bonds had come down for about four days but they seem to have found support at about seven percent," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities.

In early activity, the benchmark 30-year bond rose 14/32 to yield 6.96 percent, nearly reversing the 15/32 in losses it tallied on Monday, when the Dow industrials fell 29 points to 5694 on extremely light volume.

"Yesterday's decline was directly associated with the bond market," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. "I don't expect volume to increase that much today but we should see the market steady to higher."
The U.S. Treasury will auction $18.75 billion in two-year notes today and $12.5 billion in five-year notes tomorrow.

Market analysts have cited the auctions as a factor contributing to recent pressure in the bond market but some also noted that the current higher yield environment could help ensure the success of the auction.
At 1000 EDT/1400 GMT, the Conference Board will release the August consumer confidence index. Economists expect a reading of 104.4 compared to 107.2 in July.

The Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi/Schroder Wertheim weekly retail chain store sales report is due at 0900 EDT/1300 GMT, and at 1455 EDT/1855 GMT, Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc will release the weekly Redbook sales report.
In Tokyo, stocks edged higher in slow trade ahead of the Bank of Japan's closely watched Tankan economic survey. The Nikkei-225 rose 27 points to 20,910.
In London, U.S. shares were mostly firmer. The FTSE-100 eased 0.9 point to 3906.6.
The dollar fell to just above 107.5 yen in Tokyo but held to near 1.475 marks in quiet European trade.
The S&P 500 index future gained 1.45 to 665.65.

The New York Times Marketplace column reports that options activity in MFS Communications Co Inc picked up ahead of the company's merger announcement. However, the Times reported, one large call sale just ahead of the deal apparently cost an unidentified insitutional seller all its potential merger-related profits.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column writes that the merger pact between WorldCom Inc and MFS could foreshadow further consolidation among local access telephone service carriers.
